blocks.text: The first step towards recovery
What is Dual Diagnosis?
First Step Towards Recovery

blocks.html: Dual diagnosis is the clinical term for when someone experiences a mental health disorder and a substance use disorder at the same time. According to the National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH), approximately 9.2 million adults in the United States experienced both a mental illness and a substance use disorder in a single year. Instead of treating these issues separately, a dual diagnosis approach treats them as a single, interconnected challenge. This is crucial because mental health symptoms often drive substance use (self-medicating), and substance use almost always worsens mental health. Common combinations include:

According to the National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH), approximately 9.2 million adults in the United States experienced both a mental illness and a substance use disorder in a single year. Instead of treating these issues separately, a dual diagnosis approach treats them as a single, interconnected challenge. This is crucial because mental health symptoms often drive substance use (self-medicating), and substance use almost always worsens mental health. Common combinations include:

items: Depression & Alcoholism: Using alcohol to numb persistent sadness or hopelessness.
Anxiety & Benzodiazepine/Opioid Use: Relying on substances to manage panic attacks or social phobia.
PTSD & Polysubstance Use: Attempting to silence intrusive memories or trauma through various substances.

blocks.text: Treating the Cause, Not Just the Symptoms
Why Simultaneous Treatment is Essential

blocks.html: Treating addiction without addressing the underlying mental health disorder is like treating a physical wound while ignoring the infection, the problem will inevitably return. When mental health and substance use are treated in isolation, a revolving door of relapse often occurs because the emotional triggers for using remain active.

faqs.q: Why is integrated treatment better than traditional rehab?
faqs.a: Integrated care addresses the root causes of addiction. Treating mental health at the same time as the addiction significantly reduces the risk of relapse triggered by untreated emotional distress.

faqs.q: Can I go to treatment without losing my job?
faqs.a: Absolutely. We assist with FMLA and Short-Term Disability documentation to ensure your career is legally protected while you are in our care.

faqs.q: How long is the dual diagnosis program?
faqs.a: While the duration varies based on individual needs, most programs range from 30 to 90 days to ensure both the physical and psychological components of recovery are stabilized.

faqs.q: Does insurance cover dual diagnosis treatment?
faqs.a: Yes, most major insurance providers cover dual diagnosis care. We offer a free, no-obligation verification to help you understand your specific coverage. Call us at 817-904-2197 to learn more.

faqs.q: Will my employer find out why I am in treatment?
faqs.a: No. Under HIPAA laws, your privacy is strictly protected. We provide the medical necessity documentation required for your leave without disclosing your specific diagnosis to your employer.

faqs.q: Do you help with travel if I live outside of Dallas?
faqs.a: Yes. Our admissions team handles all travel logistics, including airport pickups from DFW or Love Field and coordination for out-of-state arrivals.

faqs.q: What therapies are used for dual diagnosis?
faqs.a: We utilize a comprehensive range of evidence-based and experiential modalities, including CBT, DBT, and EMDR for trauma, as well as individual, group, family, and equine-assisted therapy.

faqs.q: Is the facility a hospital setting?
faqs.a: No. Dallas Detox Center is a private, luxury estate designed to feel like a home. It offers premium amenities and a tranquil environment that promotes healing.

faqs.q: Can I receive treatment for just mental health without a substance issue?
faqs.a: Yes. We have a dedicated mental health treatment program designed for individuals seeking primary residential care for disorders such as depression, anxiety, or PTSD without a co-occurring addiction. Call us at 817-904-2197 to see if this program is the right solution for you or your loved one.
